conservation.report_notes: Published with corresponding artwork entry in *Georgia O’Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné* (Lynes, 1999), this historical conservation information documents treatment decisions made during the artist’s lifetime. Lynes quotes information found on backing labels, and, when noted, from other sources.

remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946." Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "On backing: In pencil by Stieglitz 'Shingle & Shell No. 3 1926 / $800' [not verified]. Also O'Keeffe initials [not verified]. Quite abstract." Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Back: O'Keeffe initials and star" [not verified]. Part of series renumbered by O'Keeffe and Doris Bry in 1970. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999: Lynes publication lists medium as 'Oil on board'. MFA Boston lists it as 'Oil on panel'. (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by MFA Boston, 2025)

credit_line: Alfred Stieglitz Collection—Bequest of Georgia O'Keeffe
description: The top of an open, white clamshell is visible at the bottom edge of the work. Behind, standing on its side, is a rough-textured, gray and black shingle. Just visible on the outer edges of the composition is a simple background of white, gray, and black geometric forms.
title: Shell and Old Shingle IV/Shell and Old Shingle No. 4
